title: Project Nightfall
description: A synthetic investigation exercise. Temporal sequence is not proof of causation.

events.event_description: Routine successful sign-in recorded before the events under review.
events.observed_behaviour: Successful sign-in from documentation address 203.0.113.10; device identifier matches the employee's usual managed laptop.
events.potential_significance: Provides a comparison point for the later unfamiliar sign-in.
events.evidence_limitations: The baseline is limited to the supplied synthetic records and does not establish a complete normal-behaviour profile.

events.event_description: Unexpected email asks the employee to review a shared document.
events.observed_behaviour: Sender is external; message contains a document-review link. No click event is included in the available evidence.
events.potential_significance: Could be a lure, routine business mail, or unrelated to later events.
events.evidence_limitations: Message body, link destination at delivery time, authentication results, and recipient interaction are not available.

events.event_description: Successful sign-in from an unfamiliar network location.
events.observed_behaviour: Sign-in from documentation address 198.51.100.24; MFA is recorded as approved. The address is not present in the short baseline.
events.potential_significance: Warrants validation with the employee and device/session telemetry.
events.evidence_limitations: An unfamiliar address and an MFA approval do not prove account compromise; travel, VPN, shared egress, and MFA-fatigue context are absent.

events.event_description: An office application started a scripting interpreter.
events.observed_behaviour: WINWORD.EXE has a child process named powershell.exe. The command line is intentionally withheld; no payload is executed by this lab.
events.potential_significance: Parent-child process context merits review and correlation with document and script-block logs.
events.evidence_limitations: Process creation alone does not establish malicious intent or what the child process did; script-block and file telemetry are unavailable.

events.event_description: Process and installed security-product inventory queries were observed.
events.observed_behaviour: A scripting process enumerated running processes and queried installed security software.
events.potential_significance: May represent host discovery, administration, inventory tooling, or unwanted activity.
events.evidence_limitations: The exact process lineage, script content, initiating user action, and prior frequency are not supplied.

events.event_description: The account accessed several documents outside its short supplied baseline.
events.observed_behaviour: Three fictional project and finance documents were opened from a new session. No download or sharing event is included.
events.potential_significance: Could be routine work or unusual access; compare with role, project assignment, session, and document audit details.
events.evidence_limitations: A limited baseline and missing business context prevent concluding that access was unauthorised or sensitive data was collected.

events.event_description: A network alert reported an unusual outbound transfer.
events.observed_behaviour: An approximately 24 MiB TLS flow to documentation address 203.0.113.77 exceeded a local volume threshold.
events.potential_significance: Requires destination ownership, process attribution, and content/context checks before assessing exfiltration.
events.evidence_limitations: Flow metadata does not reveal payload contents, destination control, business purpose, or whether the transfer contained organisational data.

events.event_description: A synthetic endpoint alert was raised for unusual office-application child-process behaviour.
events.observed_behaviour: The alert references the process relationship in E-03; its severity is medium and its automated disposition is unknown.
events.potential_significance: Provides a second sensor view of E-03 but is not independent proof of malicious activity.
events.evidence_limitations: Underlying alert rule, raw telemetry, and analyst disposition are not provided.

events.event_description: A scheduled backup process transferred data to a documentation-range internal service.
events.observed_behaviour: A 26 MiB TLS flow to 192.0.2.80 is attributed to the managed backup agent and matches its supplied schedule.
events.potential_significance: Demonstrates why volume alone is insufficient to classify E-06.
events.evidence_limitations: This record does not identify the process responsible for E-06 or establish that both flows have the same purpose.

events.event_description: The employee says the sender and document request are not familiar.
events.observed_behaviour: Employee denies knowingly opening the link at the time of the interview.
events.potential_significance: Useful lead for validating the mail event and timing, but recollection is not a substitute for telemetry.
events.evidence_limitations: Retrospective self-report may be incomplete; message interaction telemetry is not included.

events.event_description: The endpoint collector clock is reported to be approximately 45 seconds ahead.
events.observed_behaviour: Endpoint timestamps may differ from identity and cloud audit timestamps by up to 45 seconds.
events.potential_significance: Affects fine-grained correlation and event-order claims.
events.evidence_limitations: The offset is approximate and no raw time-synchronisation log is supplied.

events.event_description: A subsequent sign-in uses the expected managed-device identifier.
events.observed_behaviour: Successful sign-in from documentation address 203.0.113.10 with the usual device identifier.
events.potential_significance: Adds context for session comparison but does not explain or clear the earlier session.
events.evidence_limitations: Session tokens, device posture, and session revocation records are unavailable.
